title.label: EXACTLY What I’ve Been Searching For

content.label: Love this app. Highly motivating.

Really blown away at the little details in this app. The developers have thought of just about everything - from keeping the interface simple & focused, to displaying a thorough list of preset habits, integrating with Apple Health so that completing a task also updates your health data, and much more. Best of all, this app makes it really easy to create and stick to new habits. One feature I’m making good use of is the ability to set reminders at custom times during your day makes it easy to follow through!

One thing I’d ask to make it even better - is the ability to go beyond your goal. I’d love to set a reasonable goal but also be able to track and celebrate when I go above and beyond! It could be something as simple as enabling the option and letting you continue to tap your task after it’s already marked ‘completed’.

title.label: Editors choice? Dev must be the editor’s child

content.label: Why is there a limit on habits bruh you never heard of a scroll bar?
I usually get bored with task apps. Not this one. It really helps me stay focused. The dopamine hit with seeing things get accomplished works well for me!
Have been using it for the past few weeks and love the interface and integrations with all apple devices

I have been using the Streaks app for a while now, and it has been a game changer for me. I have always struggled with keeping up with my daily habits, but this app has made it so much easier. The app is incredibly user-friendly and the interface is easy to navigate. The sounds when I complete a task are very appealing and provide a sense of accomplishment. I also love the month view, which allows me to see which days I completed a streak and which days I need to work on. This helps me stay motivated and stay on track. Overall, I highly recommend this app to anyone looking to improve their daily habits. It gets 5 stars from me!

title.label: Love the idea, the UI is not intuitive

content.label: The whole interface is a confounding mixture of taps and long presses to accomplish the singular task of marking an activity complete. It’s terribly frustrating to try and record activity and the target cycles through three views. A long press zooms into the calendar for date adjustment or confirming completion. It’s all so complicated and somehow worse than all the swiping that’s popular with apps these days.

Love this app. I have other habit trackers, but they are not as graphical and easy to use as Streaks. I like that iCloud sync works well with my iOS and Mac devices. The degree of customization is ideal but not overly complex. I use this app every day to track my weight lifting body splits, my runs and type of runs (tempo, long, etc), coffee intake, teeth whitening, shuddering “O’s” (yea, you read that right lol), dog walks, veggies eaten, etc. The one limitation as of Jan 2022 is that there are four pages of 6 trackers each for a total of 24 activities to track maximum. This sounds generous, but it’s actually quite easy to fill. Example if one puts each body part as a lifting tracker (biceps, chest, back, etc), at least 8 activities are taken up. Please Developer, give us another page or two (5-6 pages of 6 each), begging you!  Awesome app overall. Get it!

Love the app, I rarely write reviews but this app has been super helpful in forming new habits. I have been trying to learn about 4 new habits mixed in with standard daily tasks I wanted to do and planning them all out in time slots doesn’t work for me but dynamically getting to them during a week on a specific cadence does work and this app allows me to track my performance at just about any frequency or configuration I can think of. Props to the devs and UX/UI designers on this one, very impressed and really enjoy using it.

I love this app, it has helped reinforce my habits and help hold myself accountable for daily tasks. Ive shared it with all of my friends and they all love it as well. Easy to use and motivating. It is accesible on mac, apple watch and iphone and can track a variety of positive and negative tasks efficiently and well. Its amazing!
It’s pretty tight.

I definitely fall into the camp of too lazy to write reviews, even when they are well-deserved. When the pop-up came up to rate the Streaks app, I felt compelled mostly thinking of the next person who might benefit. 

This app offers a lot so that you can really customize your experience. It has taken into account that not all goals or parameters of success are measured the same and even allows you to differentiate between the "do" goals vs. the "do not" goals (i.e. do drink 100 oz of water/day, do not drink alcohol). I know there are a lot of ways I am underutilizing this app. I think this is mostly due to the lack of instructions especially the app on your phone vs the one on my computer/Mac. 

The biggest benefit I have found is that the interface (like grouping like goals) has resulted in internal motivation. When I complete one goal, visually seeing it completed and the ones next to it not completed, tricks my mind into wanting to complete the other goals simply to check them off the list. 

One complaint I do have is not being able to (or not knowing how) to rearrange goals on different pages after they are created and I have been tracking them for a while. For example, I have a goal to journal every day and to study art for X amount of time/day. Originally, these generally seemed like they fell into a similar category; however, I recently created additional art goals like drawing 50 circles/day, drawing 50 ovals/day, etc. etc. I would like to move the journal every day on a separate page but have not figured it out and do not want to lose what I have captured by simply restarting.

title.label: Falling prey to adding complexity for the sake of complexity

content.label:
Full disclosure, I’m an experience designer but I’ve tried to separate the “academic” from my experience of the app. 

I’ve used Streaks on and off for years. I came back to it in late 2022 and my overall thought is that “less is more” has fallen a little by the wayside. For example, could you please make it “fall off a log” easy to have a view that shows all one’s tasks regardless of positive/negative/completion status?

I understand why some may want the level of filtering / number of views but honestly, I really just need to see all tasks with all statuses - and I’d bet I’m not alone. This also could increase retention with new users. Thanks!

Nice to have: a tally-like option to simply count when you did something, with no specific date or number requirements. Use case: days I went on a road trip, days I went to Target, days I went to the beach.
truly one of the best ive ever gotten for my morning routines. use this app, whatever you do.

title.label: Absolutely THE BEST for creating habits...

content.label: You can't find better. Simple. Addicting in a beneficial way. Want to start something? It'll help. Want to stop something? It'll help. Want to up your game on an already established habit, it'll help you. Want metrics? You got 'em. Use it and it will change you. Pro-Tip: use the four panel widget and put it front and center on your primary phone screen. So awesome!

As an autistic and ADHD person, I have struggled completing basic tasks (like brushing my teeth) as well as finding motivation to do chores. This app sends me reminders to do things like brush my teeth and then has a completion day count for things like chores! I’m 1 week in and have brushed my teeth twice a day for 7 days for the first time since I was probably like 8!

It’s ok. The idea is really nice and I want to use it more. But the interface is not intuitive at all. After not using it for some time I decided to try to use it again and I cannot remember how to even add a new task. I’m tapping everywhere and it’s not obvious at all. Do I really have to dive into the help tutorial to remind myself how this app works? I’m shocked it ever had rave reviews.

I love the Steaks app. It is simple enough to get started right away, persistent enough to get my attention when I have a spare moment, subtle enough that it doesn’t draw my attention away when I’m busy, and nicely designed. 

I really enjoy using the app and I find that my thinking has shifted substantially since I started using it. I entered a goal for “eat a healthy meal” and while that might seem utterly underwhelming as my target is literally *one* healthy meal at some point during the day. My focus has shifted from “what am I going to eat for lunch?” when my work schedule gets too crazy for what I had planned, to “what healthy meal will I eat today?” This has the knock on effect of generating loads of healthy meal ideas that I’m enthused about, without any real pressure. So my eating is better throughout the day. I was eating fast food at least 3x/week before. I got fast food once in the last two weeks. Not perfect, but definitely progress I’m happy with.

I’ve set similarly effective goals for quality time with my kids, maintaining other relationships, and exercise. Some goals I don’t hit everyday, but I’m making progress on those too.

So glad I got this app. Best $5 I’ve spent in a long time.

This App is a god send for me. It has helped me to carve out habits. I have read so many books on self help and habit forming but this app brought it all together for me. Love it. I wish there was a way to add more streaks but I believe I can creatively work around this restriction

I love this app so far and would gladly give it 5 stars, but just don’t understand why there is a limit of 24 habits?  In this day of elastic computing and given the design of 6 habits per card, why can’t we just have a 5th or 6th or frankly unlimited habits?

I want to track specific things I want to do every day…like make my bed, run the dishwasher, cuddle with my wife, etc.  but quickly my 24 habits are consumed, but I probably have anywhere from from 12-24 more I want to track.  

Can someone explain why there is this seemingly artificial constraint?

title.label: The best—and no subscription BUT AVOID MAC VERSION

content.label:
UPDATE 2022-11-26: I made major changes to my habits—changing some existing ones and added new ones on my phone—his morning. I hadn't used my MacBook in a few days, and after using it I realized that instead of syncing all of my latest changes from my phone to my MBP, Streaks did the opposite and replaced all the work I'd done today with the days-old versions from my Mac. I'm still leaving my 5 star rave review on the iOS app store because I really like Streaks, but I've already deleted the app from my Mac.  

REQUEST: Please allow longer task labels—I often struggle to abbreviate them!  

REVIEW: Streaks does the job with style and flair. Love the design, and once you figure out how the settings work, it’s very easy to use. (If you don’t like the orange, it’s simple to change the colors of the interface and the icon.) The ability to archive habits is a nice touch, so if you decide to start one up again in the future, you don’t have to begin from scratch. I mostly use Streaks on my phone, but it’s nice having it on my Mac, too, where I leave it running mostly as a reminder and for when I’m working and leave my phone out of reach. I’ll never pay a recurring subscription to use a habit app. Fortunately, the best one in the App Store doesn’t require one.

content.label: It would be great if we can shake to undo on watch, or undo last completion on iPhone.
I find this app more and more annoying on MacOS. I quit it and it reopens whenever it wants. Stop popping up in front of the window I'm working in.

title.label: Long-time user request for infrequent tasks

content.label: I love this app but wish it had one made change. If a task if set to be done only 2 times in a month, or on Fridays in a week, I want the circle to *stay* filled in to show me I have completed it for that week or month. I'm done. The biggest thing that keeps me motivated is filling in the circles. But if I have a weekly task or monthly task, it will only stay filled in for the day I compelete it. But then the next day it "looks" incomplete because the circle is open again. Please find a way to address this!
Started using streaks a couple years ago.  Covid took me away.  Just came back to it and really like the expanded capabilities.  On day 6 of my current multiple streaks.  Love it!
Just what I needed. About a week in and I am loving how I have gamified my habits!
